QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_1

question.text: Which legislative development brought Social Impact Assessment under the purview of compliance for Indian corporates, specifically requiring impact assessments for certain CSR projects?

answer.text: Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Amendment Rules, 2020, insertion of sub-rule (3) to rule 8
SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015 Part VII amendment introducing BRSR disclosures
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2006 social-audit clause
SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018 Chapter X-A insertion in 2022

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.1 of the workbook is explicit: the Companies (CSR Policy) Amendment Rules 2020 inserted sub-rule (3) to rule 8, requiring companies with average CSR obligation of INR 10 crore or more in the three preceding financial years to undertake impact assessment for CSR projects with outlays of INR 1 crore or more that are at least one year old. That is what formally brought SIA into Indian corporate compliance. The Trap: LODR Part VII (Option B) is about BRSR reporting for top-1000 listed entities, not CSR impact assessment. MNREGA (Option C) introduced Gram-Sabha social audits at panchayat level, not corporate SIA. ICDR Chapter X-B (Option D) created the SSE framework and empanelment of SIAs but the CSR impact-assessment trigger itself came through the 2020 CSR Rules amendment. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser) tests CSR advisory framing; NISM V-A (MF Distributor) tests the 80G donor-side. XXIII is uniquely the SIA-certifier lens on the same CSR impact-assessment universe. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When scoping a CSR impact engagement, first triage whether the funding corporate falls within rule 8(3) — only then is the assessment mandatory. A company with INR 9.8 crore three-year average CSR is outside the trigger even if an individual project crossed INR 1 crore.
